job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: Last Sunday, Rohan and his younger sister Meera woke up before dawn to join their uncle, Mr. Gupta, for a bird-watching walk at Sultanpur Lake. The air was crisp and cool as they walked along the muddy path. Mr. Gupta carried a heavy pair of binoculars and a notebook to record their sightings. They spotted 12 different species of birds near the water's edge. Rohan was excited to see a kingfisher, but Meera was more interested in the tall reeds swaying in the breeze. Because the water level had dropped significantly during the dry summer, the birds gathered closer to the center of the lake to find food. Mr. Gupta explained that the birds migrate thousands of miles to escape the harsh winters of the north. By 9:00 AM, the sun was high, and the children felt exhausted from the long trek. They decided to head home for a warm breakfast, promising to return when the monsoon rains arrived. It was a memorable morning for the family, filled with quiet observations and the chirping of hidden creatures.
response.summary: Rohan, Meera, and their uncle visited Sultanpur Lake early in the morning to observe migratory birds. They saw many species and learned why the birds were gathered in the center of the lake. The group returned home by mid-morning after a successful bird-watching trip.
